resource.description: Track-authored patient-based proportion of eligible community-dwelling adults aged 65 or older seen in ambulatory care during the measurement period who have a completed three-question STEADI screen. Not CMS139FHIR and not claimed equivalent to it.
resource.guidance: Synthetic Connectathon context only: community residence and exclusion of hospice, inpatient and long-term-care settings are supplied by the track context; AMB does not prove residence or hospice status. Age is calculated at the linked encounter start. A completed screen requires status completed and one usable Boolean answer for each required linkId in one response. Explicit false is complete; absent or incomplete responses do not enter the numerator. The measure counts a patient once when any linked eligible encounter has a completed screen within the period.
resource.disclaimer: Connectathon testing and education only. No clinical approval or CMS139FHIR equivalence is claimed.

resource.title: Exercise and rate of incident falls
resource.description:
Intervention: exercise-interventions. Comparator: trial-comparator. Outcome: incident-fall-rate.

Exercise versus contributing trial comparator arms: incidence rate ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.75 to 0.96), 29 trials, 14,475 participants, longest follow-up 6 to 24 months. Heterogeneity I-squared = 82.7% (supplied AHRQ abstract). This estimate applies to incident fall rate, not the number of people who fall.

Recommendation grade B: The USPSTF recommends exercise interventions for community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older at increased fall risk.

USPSTF assessed moderate certainty of a moderate net benefit for its recommendation. This is not a certainty rating assigned by this implementation to the individual pooled estimate.

Harms: About half of exercise trials reported harms. Minor musculoskeletal symptoms were most common; serious harms were rare, with exercise-associated wrist and hip fractures reported in separate trials. Sparse reporting limits certainty about harms.

Limitations: Interventions, baseline risks and follow-up varied. The evidence does not select one best exercise regimen. Lack of statistically significant fracture or mortality reductions does not establish no effect.

resource.title: Multifactorial intervention and rate of incident falls
resource.description:
Intervention: multifactorial-interventions. Comparator: trial-comparator. Outcome: incident-fall-rate.

Multifactorial intervention versus contributing trial comparator arms: incidence rate ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.74 to 0.95), 20 trials, 22,115 participants, longest follow-up 6 to 28 months. Heterogeneity I-squared = 85.0% (supplied AHRQ abstract). This estimate applies to incident fall rate, not the number of people who fall.

Recommendation grade C: The USPSTF recommends individualizing whether to offer multifactorial interventions to community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older at increased fall risk, considering prior falls, comorbidities and patient preferences.

USPSTF assessed moderate certainty of a small net benefit for its recommendation. Routine provision to everyone is not the recommended decision.

Harms: Harms were sparsely reported; five trials with 4,199 participants reported generally rare, minor effects, often associated with exercise components.

Limitations: Trial components, baseline risks, implementation and adherence varied. Pooled results did not establish statistically significant reductions in people falling, injurious falls, fractures or mortality; this is not proof of no effect.
